headline: ### 1. Broad Market Index Performance & Technical Action.
summary: ### 1. Broad Market Index Performance & Technical Action.

indexes.name: Dow Jones Industrial Average
indexes.action: Roared over 3% higher (surging more than 1,500 to 1,600 points), led by massive gains in blue-chip stocks to close near session highs well above recent trading ranges.

indexes.name: S&P 500 (SPY)
indexes.action: Advanced 1.6%, closing in the upper half of its daily range directly at its 50-day moving average line. The move registered as an accumulation day backed by expanding volume on the New York Stock Exchange.

indexes.name: NASDAQ Composite
indexes.action: Gained 1.4%, but remained the weakest of the major benchmarks as early momentum faded into overhead resistance at moving averages following a bounce off its 200-day moving average line.

indexes.name: Russell 2000 (Small Caps)
indexes.action: Added 1.5%, attempting to reclaim its 50-day moving average line and returning to levels where it stood four trading sessions prior.

indexes.name: Market Character & Breadth
indexes.action: Driven by a powerful relief rally following the conclusion of the midterm elections. Aside from semiconductor and AI names, market leadership broadened significantly across cyclical, financial, and consumer sectors.

macro.title: Midterm Election Results
macro.text: The market responded positively to the removal of election uncertainty as Democrats flipped key seats (including a historic shift in Texas), establishing political gridlock that investors historically favor.

macro.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Collapse
macro.text: Yields fell sharply below 4.9% (down ~6 basis points to 4.88%–4.89%), easing interest rate pressures across equities.

macro.title: Crude Oil Plunge (USO)
macro.text: Crude oil proxy USO dropped 8%, breaking back below its 50-day moving average line shortly after a breakout attempt, providing immediate relief for transportation and consumer discretionary stocks.

macro.title: AI & Data Center Regulatory Fears
macro.text: Concerns over potential regulatory moratoriums on data center construction and tighter capital expenditure oversight weighed heavily on memory makers and specialized data center operators like CoreWeave and SpaceX.

sectors.name: Semiconductors (SMH) & Memory Breakdown
sectors.action: The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) dropped 2.8% to 3.0%. DRAM and memory stocks suffered heavy distribution, plunging 5.3% on the day.

sectors.name: Financials (XLF)
sectors.action: Surged 3.5% to new highs, highlighted by JPMorgan Chase (JPM) retaking its 50-day moving average line and BlackRock (BLK) executing a clean technical breakout.

sectors.name: Consumer Discretionary (XLY) & Retail (XRT)
sectors.action: XLY jumped 6.0% (propelled by a 6% advance in Amazon), while the Retail ETF (XRT) surged 5.5% amid broad strength across retail apparel.

sectors.name: Consumer Staples (XLP)
sectors.action: Gained 3.4% as institutional flows entered defensive growth names.

sectors.name: Homebuilders (ITB) & Airlines (JETS)
sectors.action: Lower 10-year yields sparked strong buying in homebuilders (ITB), while airlines and online travel providers (such as Expedia) rallied ahead of earnings.

stocks.action: Technical Action: Surged 3.5%, clearing a high-handle consolidation just below the 400 round number to offer an alternate entry point within a valid buy zone. | Fundamentals: Boasts an IBD Composite Rating of 99, supported by solid top- and bottom-line Q3 earnings growth and a Relative Strength (RS) line reaching new highs.

Technical Action: Surged 5.3% on a massive volume expansion (>100% above average), staging a strong weekly upside reversal back to all-time highs despite an early morning dip below its 50-day line; added to the Leaderboard model portfolio. | Fundamentals: Institutional buyers favored Apple due to its conservative AI capital expenditure approach and strong cash position compared to cash-burning hyperscale peers.

Technical Action: Advanced 6.0%, clearing a trendline entry within its base and resistance above the 240 level amid strong discount retail momentum. | Strategy: Heading into earnings next week, analysts highlight ROST as a potential candidate for a call option trade given its strong chart setup and RS line.
Gapped up 8% in pre-market trading following strong quarterly earnings, but gave back all gains during regular hours to close flat as chip sector selling intensified.

strategy.title: Day 2 of Rally Attempt
strategy.text: Wednesday marked Day 2 of a new rally attempt for both the NASDAQ Composite and the S&P 500 (with Tuesday representing Day 1).

strategy.title: Follow-Through Day (FTD) Requirements
strategy.text: A valid Follow-Through Day requires a strong index gain on higher volume and can occur no earlier than Day 4 of the rally attempt.

strategy.title: Allowing Short Covering to Clear
strategy.text: Waiting until Day 4 or later ensures that initial short-covering bounces clear out before committing fresh capital.

strategy.title: Key Low Support Level
strategy.text: The rally attempt remains intact as long as the recent benchmark low (established just above the 200-day moving average line) is not undercut.

strategy.text: Historical data from the Stock Trader's Almanac points to strong end-of-year and post-midterm election seasonality for equities. 📊 Would you like to turn these chart setups and rally attempt rules into an interactive quiz or flashcards to test your technical analysis knowledge?

macro.text: The iShares U.S. Home Construction ETF (ITB) dropped 3.6%, getting turned away directly at resistance at its 200-day moving average line.

macro.text: Investor focus remains locked on midterm election results, with prediction markets showing a 70%–75% probability of Democrats winning the Senate and a >90% probability of taking the House.

sectors.action: Advanced 2.0% to recover toward its 200-day moving average line, but the move came on lighter volume and met early technical resistance, indicating a low-conviction bounce.

Technical Action & Setup: World's largest methanol producer sitting right at the top of a base in buy range following a strong post-earnings surge. | Fundamentals: Supported by massive quarterly bottom-line earnings percentage growth and an upward-trending Relative Strength (RS) line near highs.

Technical Action: Bounced off support at its 21-day moving average line post-earnings to reclaim its buy point, accompanied by an RS line reaching new highs. | Peer Action: Marriott (MAR) exhibits a similar high-quality setup near highs.

Gapped below its 50-day moving average line due to lower holiday quarter margin guidance caused by elevated memory input costs.

Arista jumped 9% after-hours off its 200-day moving average line, while SMCI rose 7%–8% after-hours to test its 200-day line ($3,267). | Jackson Financial: Executed an actionable breakout ahead of earnings with an RS line "blue dot".

headline: ### 1. Broad Market Index Performance & Technical Action.
summary: ### 1. Broad Market Index Performance & Technical Action.

indexes.name: NASDAQ Composite
indexes.action: Hardest hit among the main indexes, falling 1.1% in a bearish outside day that closed at the bottom of its daily range. The Composite is now down more than 9% from its highs, nearing a 10% mid-range correction and coming down to test its critical 200-day moving average line after breaking prior support levels.

indexes.name: NASDAQ 100 (QQQ)
indexes.action: Plunged 1.4%, taking out earlier support near the 700 level and reaching the 10% correction mark, with its 200-day line serving as the next logical floor.

indexes.name: S&P 500
indexes.action: Closed down 0.5%, dropping back below its 50-day moving average line. While support at the 750 level held for the session and the index maintains cushion above its 200-day line, it has failed to sustain higher technical support levels.

indexes.name: Russell 2000 (Small Caps)
indexes.action: Ended down fractionally after failing a bounce attempt off its 200-day moving average line. Small caps remain in a "ping-pong" range between their 50-day and 200-day moving average lines awaiting a decisive directional breakout.

indexes.name: Dow Jones Industrial Average
indexes.action: Outperformed other major benchmarks by closing up 0.4%, though it finished well below its session highs.

indexes.name: Equal-Weight S&P 500 (RSP) & Midcaps (MDY)
indexes.action: Midcaps (MDY) rose 0.75%. The equal-weight RSP closed stable, highlighting that the average stock is holding up far better than market-cap-weighted indexes dragged down by mega-cap technology.

macro.title: Crude Oil & Treasury Yield Pullback
macro.text: Crude oil proxy USO fell 7%, while the 10-year Treasury yield pulled back noticeably from recent peaks.

macro.title: Intermarket Disconnect
macro.text: Falling bond yields and declining oil prices typically fuel equity rallies, but broader market sentiment was overridden by AI spending concerns, potential technology regulatory risks, and caution surrounding upcoming midterm elections.

macro.title: Home Construction & Transportation Response
macro.text: Lower interest rates boosted homebuilders (ITB), which reclaimed its 200-day moving average line. Lower fuel costs supported transportation and leisure names, driving the airline ETF (JETS) up 4% to test its 200-day line behind strength in Delta Air Lines (DAL).

sectors.name: Magnificent 7 Drag (MAGS)
sectors.action: The Magnificent 7 ETF (MAGS) suffered heavy selling, acting as the primary weight pulling down major market-cap weighted indexes.

sectors.name: Software & Cybersecurity Reversals
sectors.action: Growth areas that had recently made progress—including cybersecurity ETFs (HACK and BUG)—faced sharp rug-pull reversals, with HACK pulling back directly to test its 50-day moving average line.

sectors.name: Defensive Flight to Safety
sectors.action: Institutional capital rotated into defensive groups, including Utilities, Food & Beverage (PBJ), Consumer Staples, and Leisure/Entertainment (PEJ).

sectors.name: Medical Growth Instability
sectors.action: While large-cap growth names like Eli Lilly (LLY) continue to hold up constructively, several medical research and services stocks (such as Natera, Grail, and Guardant Health) suffered sharp downside breaks.

stocks.action: Technical & Setup Action: Forming the right side of a bottoming base as the business transitions toward its first expected year of profitability. Its Relative Strength (RS) line broke a multi-month downtrend, backed by a 3-month RS rating of 92 and a 6-month RS rating of 85. | Fundamentals: Generated 150% bottom-line earnings growth in its most recent quarterly report.

Technical Action: Advanced 5% post-earnings, displaying strong relative strength (3-month RS of 87, 6-month RS of 92). | Catalyst & Resistance: Driven by the appointment of a new CEO. Traders are monitoring overhead supply and resistance levels around 75 and 80 on the weekly chart.

Technical Action: Advanced 5.4%, building the right side of a base above a flattening 200-day moving average line following a mild 20% correction. | Fundamentals: Posted accelerating quarterly EPS growth over four quarters (2%, 51%, 33%, 24%, and 39%) accompanied by solid double-digit top-line revenue growth. Key overhead resistance lies just ahead.

strategy.title: Prudent Cash Preservation
strategy.text: Raising cash levels and taking a defensive posture is warranted when drawdowns expand and broad market support levels break, especially given upcoming midterm election and earnings catalysts.

strategy.title: Waiting for Market Traction
strategy.text: Avoid forcing trades during severe market pullbacks; wait for individual holdings to show traction or for a confirmed follow-through day (which can occur in as few as 4 days) before aggressively deploying capital.

strategy.title: Screening Short-Term Relative Strength
strategy.text: During rotational markets, evaluate short-term 3-month and 6-month RS ratings to spot emerging sector leaders, while mapping out overhead supply on weekly charts to identify potential resistance zones. 📈 Would you like to turn these chart setups and market risk rules into an interactive quiz or study flashcards?

headline: ### 1. Broad Market Index Performance & Technical Action.
summary: ### 1. Broad Market Index Performance & Technical Action.

indexes.name: NASDAQ Composite
indexes.action: Tumbled 2.9%, suffering severe damage as it broke decisively below the 26,000 support level. The tech-heavy NASDAQ 100 led declines, plunging 3.5%. Both indexes are magnetizing toward their critical 200-day moving average lines, placing the market in a precarious technical state.

indexes.name: S&P 500
indexes.action: Fell 1.8%, undercutting key technical support levels. It tested horizontal support around 7,496 (its September 16 low), with the 200-day moving average line (~7,290) serving as the next major line in the sand.

indexes.name: Dow Jones Industrial Average
indexes.action: Dropped 1.1%, exhibiting relatively milder downside compared to tech benchmarks.

indexes.name: Russell 2000 (Small Caps)
indexes.action: Declined 1.7%, getting rejected at its 50-day moving average line as mid-cap (MDY) and small-cap indexes failed to hold technical breakouts.

indexes.name: Equal-Weight S&P 500 (RSP) & Market Breadth
indexes.action: The RSP fell only 0.8%, holding up significantly better than market-cap-weighted indexes. The RSP maintains a healthy cup-with-handle breakout structure and stacked short-term moving averages ("rainbow order"), indicating that the average stock is faring better than mega-cap technology leaders.

macro.title: Post-Regulation FD Earnings Volatility
macro.text: Under Regulation FD, corporate earnings surprises produce extreme quarterly price gaps (both up and down) across institutional stocks because selective information is no longer leaked to major players ahead of time.

macro.title: Upcoming Catalysts & Federal Reserve Context

strategy.title: Preserving Cash
strategy.text: Entering a 100% cash position during severe distribution removes market noise, protects capital, and allows investors to evaluate setups with fresh eyes.

strategy.title: Waiting for a Follow-Through Day (FTD)
strategy.text: Before aggressively committing capital, wait for a distinct rally day followed four or more days later by a confirmed Follow-Through Day (a sharp index gain on higher volume).

strategy.title: Respecting the 200-Day Line
strategy.text: Treat the 200-day moving average as the single most critical baseline for index and individual stock health—historically, healthy advances occur above it, while major damage happens below it.

strategy.title: Quicksand RS Line Exit Rules
strategy.text: Monitor the RS line against Fibonacci moving averages (8, 13, 21 on weekly charts). When the RS line drops below the final moving average, treat it as an objective signal to sell and protect capital. 💡 Would you like to turn these market index support levels and RS line exit rules into an interactive study quiz or flashcards?

sections.title: Broad Market Index Performance & Technical Action

items.title: NASDAQ Composite
items.text: Tumbled 2.9%, suffering severe damage as it broke decisively below the 26,000 support level. The tech-heavy NASDAQ 100 led declines, plunging 3.5%. Both indexes are magnetizing toward their critical 200-day moving average lines, placing the market in a precarious technical state.

items.title: S&P 500
items.text: Fell 1.8%, undercutting key technical support levels. It tested horizontal support around 7,496 (its September 16 low), with the 200-day moving average line (~7,290) serving as the next major line in the sand.

items.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average
items.text: Dropped 1.1%, exhibiting relatively milder downside compared to tech benchmarks.

items.title: Russell 2000 (Small Caps)
items.text: Declined 1.7%, getting rejected at its 50-day moving average line as mid-cap (MDY) and small-cap indexes failed to hold technical breakouts.

items.title: Equal-Weight S&P 500 (RSP) & Market Breadth
items.text: The RSP fell only 0.8%, holding up significantly better than market-cap-weighted indexes. The RSP maintains a healthy cup-with-handle breakout structure and stacked short-term moving averages ("rainbow order"), indicating that the average stock is faring better than mega-cap technology leaders.
